BotServ keeps service bots for your chan: BotServ keeps service bots for your channels: assign a bot, speak through it, and configure kickers, badwords, and triggers.
ChanFix recovers opless channels from ac: ChanFix recovers opless channels from accumulated op-time. It defers to ChanServ and won't touch a registered channel. Operator-only.
ChanServ registers and looks after chann: ChanServ registers and looks after channels. Register a channel you hold ops in, then manage its access, modes, and topic.
DebugServ streams live services activity: DebugServ streams live services activity — authentication, sessions, and the account/channel/operator lifecycle — to the staff log channel.
DiceServ rolls dice and evaluates maths: DiceServ rolls dice and evaluates maths for tabletop games. Dice: 2d6, d20, d%. Also + - * / ^ %, parentheses, functions (sqrt, floor, min, ...), pi/e, and 3~2d6 to repeat.
DictServ looks words up in the dict.org: DictServ looks words up in the dict.org dictionaries. Try dict <word> (WordNet), define (GCIDE), thes (thesaurus), acronym, element, law, bible, and more — LOOKUP lists them all.
GamesServ referees \u0002tic-tac-toe\u00: GamesServ referees tic-tac-toe, Connect Four and chess — it checks every move and keeps a ranked ladder. Challenge someone, then take turns. Moves: ttt cell 0-8, c4 column 0-6, chess UCI (e2e4).
GroupServ manages user groups: a \u0002!: GroupServ manages user groups: a !name owning member accounts. Add a group to a channel's access (/msg ChanServ ACCESS #chan ADD !name op) and each member holding the group's c flag inherits it.
HelpServ is the help desk and the networ: HelpServ is the help desk and the network's help index. Open a ticket with REQUEST; operators work the queue.
HostServ gives you a virtual host (vhost: HostServ gives you a virtual host (vhost). Activate an assigned one, pick one from the menu, or request one from an operator.
InfoServ holds the network's information: InfoServ holds the network's information bulletins: public ones show on connect, oper ones on login.
MemoServ delivers messages to registered: MemoServ delivers messages to registered users, online or not. You must be identified to use it.
NickServ looks after your nickname and a: NickServ looks after your nickname and account: register it, identify to it, and manage its settings.
OperServ holds the network operator tool: OperServ holds the network operator tools. Every command is operator-only.
ReportServ takes abuse reports. Anyone c: ReportServ takes abuse reports. Anyone can REPORT; operators review the queue.
StatServ reports statistics: \u0002SERVE: StatServ reports statistics: SERVER for network-wide counters (operators), or a #channel for its activity (founder).

Syntax: \u0002SET PASSWORD <new>\u0002,:
Syntax: SET PASSWORD <new>, SET EMAIL <address>, SET PUBKEY [key], SET GREET [message], SET AVATAR|BIO|PRONOUNS|TIMEZONE|URL [value], SET AUTOOP {ON|OFF}, SET KILL {ON|OFF}, or SET HIDE STATUS {ON|OFF}
Changes your password, email, public key, greet, public profile, auto-op, nick-protection, or last-seen privacy. SET PUBKEY stores a NIST P-256 public key (base64 SEC1 point) so you can log in with the ECDSA-NIST256P-CHALLENGE SASL mechanism instead of a password; give no value to clear it. Syntax: \u0002SET PUBKEY <key>\u0002 (g:
Syntax: SET PUBKEY <key>  (give no key to clear it)
Stores a NIST P-256 public key on your account so you can log in with the ECDSA-NIST256P-CHALLENGE SASL mechanism instead of a password. At login the server sends a random challenge, your client signs it with the matching private key, and the signature is verified against the stored key — so the private key never leaves your client and this is safe even without TLS.
The key is the base64 SEC1 point. Generate one with openssl: openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out ~/.ecdsa.pem, then openssl ec -in ~/.ecdsa.pem -pubout -conv_form compressed -outform DER 2>/dev/null | tail -c 33 | base64 — give that printed value to SET PUBKEY and point your client's SASL key setting at ~/.ecdsa.pem. SET PUBKEY with no argument removes it.
